Divergences between Gaussian and complex Wishart models

Source: R/divergences.R
divergences.Rd

Closed-form divergences between two multivariate normal laws \(N_p(\mu_1, \Sigma_1)\) and \(N_p(\mu_2, \Sigma_2)\), and between two scaled complex Wishart laws \(\mathcal{W}_m(\Sigma_1, L)\) and \(\mathcal{W}_m(\Sigma_2, L)\) with a common number of looks. They are the building blocks of the divergence-based classifiers of Ferreira, Coelho and Nascimento (2021).

Usage

divergence_gaussian(
  mu1,
  Sigma1,
  mu2,
  Sigma2,
  type = c("kl", "jeffreys", "bhattacharyya", "renyi"),
  order = 0.5,
  kind = 1
)

divergence_wishart(
  Sigma1,
  Sigma2,
  L,
  type = c("kl", "jeffreys", "bhattacharyya", "renyi"),
  order = 0.5,
  kind = 1
)

Arguments

mu1, mu2

Mean vectors.

Sigma1, Sigma2

Covariance matrices (real symmetric for Gaussian laws, Hermitian for Wishart laws).

type

Divergence: "kl", "jeffreys", "bhattacharyya" or "renyi".

order

Order \(\alpha \in (0, 1)\) of the Rényi divergence.

kind

Form of the Rényi divergence (1 to 4).

L

Number of looks (common to both Wishart laws).

Value

A single non-negative number.

Details

Available measures (type):

"kl"

Kullback-Leibler divergence \(D_{KL}(\theta_1 \| \theta_2)\).

"jeffreys"

Jeffreys divergence \(D_{KL}(\theta_1 \| \theta_2) + D_{KL}(\theta_2 \| \theta_1)\).

"bhattacharyya"

Bhattacharyya distance \(-\log \int \sqrt{f_1 f_2}\).

"renyi"

Rényi divergence of order \(\alpha\) (order), in one of four forms (kind): 1, \(D^\alpha_R(\theta_1\|\theta_2)\); 2, \(D^\alpha_R(\theta_2\|\theta_1)\); 3, the symmetrised mean \([D^\alpha_R(\theta_1\|\theta_2) + D^\alpha_R(\theta_2\|\theta_1)]/2\); and 4, \(c \log\{[K(\theta_1\|\theta_2) + K(\theta_2\|\theta_1)]/2\}\), where \(K(\theta_1\|\theta_2) = \int f_1^\alpha f_2^{1-\alpha}\).

For Gaussian laws the Rényi divergence uses the normalisation of Pardo (2006), \(c = 1/[\alpha(\alpha - 1)]\), which gives $$D^\alpha_R = \frac{1}{2}\Delta^\top M^{-1}\Delta - \frac{1}{2\alpha(\alpha-1)}\log\frac{|M|}{|\Sigma_1|^{1-\alpha} |\Sigma_2|^{\alpha}},$$ with \(\Delta = \mu_1 - \mu_2\) and \(M = \alpha\Sigma_2 + (1-\alpha)\Sigma_1\). For Wishart laws the normalisation of Frery, Nascimento and Cintra (2014), \(c = 1/(\alpha - 1)\), is used: $$D^\alpha_R = \frac{L}{\alpha - 1}\log\frac{|(\alpha\Sigma_1^{-1} + (1-\alpha)\Sigma_2^{-1})^{-1}|}{|\Sigma_1|^\alpha|\Sigma_2|^{1-\alpha}}.$$ Both converge to the Kullback-Leibler divergence when \(\alpha \to 1\).

References

Ferreira, J. A., Coelho, H. and Nascimento, A. D. C. (2021). A family of divergence-based classifiers for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) imagery vector and matrix features. International Journal of Remote Sensing, 42(4), 1201–1229. doi:10.1080/01431161.2020.1826060

Frery, A. C., Nascimento, A. D. C. and Cintra, R. J. (2014). Analytic expressions for stochastic distances between relaxed complex Wishart distributions. IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, 52(2), 1213–1226.

Pardo, L. (2006). Statistical Inference Based on Divergence Measures. Chapman & Hall/CRC.

Examples

S1 <- diag(3); S2 <- diag(c(2, 1, 0.5))
divergence_gaussian(c(0, 0, 0), S1, c(1, 0, 0), S2, type = "kl")
#> [1] 0.5
divergence_gaussian(c(0, 0, 0), S1, c(1, 0, 0), S2, type = "renyi",
                    order = 0.5, kind = 3)
#> [1] 0.5688994

W1 <- polsar_example_sigma("forest"); W2 <- polsar_example_sigma("urban")
divergence_wishart(W1, W2, L = 4, type = "jeffreys")
#> [1] 11.28573
divergence_wishart(W1, W2, L = 4, type = "renyi", order = 0.9)
#> [1] 3.368488
